Lesson · 20 min

Working with Microsoft Office Files

Open and edit Word, Excel, and PowerPoint files without converting them, convert one to a Google file when you need to, and download Google files as Office files or PDFs.

By the end of this lesson you can

  • ✓Open and edit a Word, Excel, or PowerPoint file from Drive and keep it in its Office format
  • ✓Convert an Office file with File › Save as Google Docs, Sheets, or Slides, and explain why that makes a copy
  • ✓Download a Google file as a Microsoft Office file or a PDF
  • ✓Choose the right format to send to someone outside your company

Lesson Notes

Read through the key concepts before you try the challenge.

Office files keep arriving

On the job

You handle the paperwork that comes into the Parkview office.

Not everyone uses Google Workspace. Russo Plumbing emails its invoices as Excel files, the lease renewal notice came from the company lawyer as a Word file, and a tenant who uses Word asked for the move-in checklist in Word. Parkview's files live in Drive, so you need to handle all of these without retyping anything.

Your task: Edit Office files in Drive, convert them when you need Google features, and send people the format they can use.

Drive stores any kind of file. When you double-click a Word, Excel, or PowerPoint file in Drive, it opens in Google Docs, Sheets, or Slides. You can read it, edit it, and comment on it. Your changes are saved back to the original Office file.

Office editing: keep the Office format

  • An Office file shows its file type in a small chip next to the name at the top left, such as .DOCX, .XLSX, or .PPTX.
  • Edits save automatically, in the Office format. Someone who downloads the file later gets a normal Word, Excel, or PowerPoint file.
  • Drive's Office editing works with Word (.doc, .docx, .dot), Excel (.xls, .xlsx, .xlsm, .xlt), and PowerPoint (.ppt, .pptx, .pps, .pot) files.

Some features work only in Google files, such as protected ranges in Sheets, add-ons, Apps Script, and translating a document. To use them, convert the file: open it, then choose File › Save as Google Docs (or Save as Google Sheets, Save as Google Slides).

Converting makes a copy. The original Office file stays in Drive, unchanged, and the new Google file opens in a new tab. Rename or delete the one you do not need so coworkers do not edit the wrong copy.

Download as Office or PDF

To send someone a file they can open without Google, download it in another format: open the file and choose File › Download, then pick the format. The download goes to your computer's Downloads folder, and you can attach it to an email. The file in Drive does not change.

Worked example

The lease renewal notice

The lawyer sent Lease Renewal Notice.docx. Denise wants it styled like Parkview's other notices and kept as a Google Doc, and a tenant needs a copy to print.

  1. 1

    Double-click the .docx file in Drive.

    It opens in Docs with the .DOCX chip, so you can check it right away without converting.

  2. 2

    File › Save as Google Docs.

    Denise wants a Google Doc, and converting gives you a Google copy while the lawyer's original stays as it was.

  3. 3

    Format the Google copy.

    Edits now go into Parkview's Google Doc, not the lawyer's file.

  4. 4

    File › Download › PDF Document (.pdf) for the tenant.

    A PDF prints the same on any computer and cannot be changed by accident.

Result: A Google Doc for the office and a PDF for the tenant, with the lawyer's original untouched.

🔑 Edit Office files in place when you only need a quick change; convert when Parkview will keep and maintain the file.

Challenge

Apply what you've learned in this lesson.

Practice with your own Google account and any Word file (or download one of your Google Docs as Word first).

  1. Upload a Word file to My Drive (New › File upload), or create a Google Doc and download it with File › Download › Microsoft Word (.docx), then upload that .docx.
  2. Double-click the Word file in Drive. Find the .DOCX chip next to the name.
  3. Make one small change, then choose File › Save as Google Docs. Check that Drive now has both files.
  4. In the Google Doc, choose File › Download › PDF Document (.pdf). Open the PDF from your Downloads folder.
Deliverable: Submit a screenshot of Drive showing both the Word file and the Google Doc, plus the PDF, to your instructor or course folder. No Google account? Complete the practice simulation and submit its results page.
